rationale: This replaces Pearson correlations with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariance matrices. The reference point is the Riemannian mean of the training fold's matrices. This was the strongest classic pipeline on ABIDE (Abraham 2017): it whitens each subject's connectome against the group geometry, which tends to reduce noise shared by the whole group and site/scanner effects while keeping individual differences. FC-region time series with zero signal get a unit diagonal so every matrix stays positive-definite. I haven't run this version, so its Dev score is unknown.

Scanner and protocol differences between ABIDE sites make each site's covariance matrices cluster around their own mean, and the scoring is done within each site. So I re-center each site's Ledoit-Wolf covariances on that site's Riemannian mean (C → M_s^{-1/2} C M_s^{-1/2}, which is Riemannian Procrustes re-centering) and then take the tangent space at the identity. This removes the site effect in the feature geometry before the linear classifier. The site means use no labels, which the brief allows for harmonization. I haven't run this version, so its Dev score is unknown.

I'm replacing the single CC200 model with an equal-weight ensemble over three parcellations: data-driven CC200 and CC400, plus anatomical AAL. Each atlas gets the same Ledoit-Wolf, per-site re-centering, tangent-space and logistic-regression pipeline as now. The atlases make partly independent errors from parcellation noise, and averaging across atlases was among the most reliable gains in Abraham 2017. Each atlas's L2 strength is scaled to its feature count, so its regularization stays comparable to the CC200 model that worked. I haven't run this, so its Dev score is unknown.

The multi-atlas ensemble timed out, so I'm going back to the single CC200 pipeline and adding one cheap harmonization step. Sites differ in timepoint count, TR and noise, so the spread of tangent vectors around each site's mean differs too, and re-centering alone doesn't fix that. The new step standardizes each tangent feature within each site, scaling it by the site's standard deviation pulled toward the pooled one. This is a ComBat-like, label-free version of the "stretch" step in Riemannian Procrustes analysis, and it puts every site's connectivity deviations on a common scale before the classifier. I haven't run it, so its Dev score is unknown.

Global signal regression (GSR) is the most disputed preprocessing choice in ABIDE. With GSR, connectivity estimates are less affected by motion and physiological noise, but the correlation structure gets shifted. That makes errors from the `filt_global` and `filt_noglobal` CC200 pipelines partly independent. I'm running the kept pipeline unchanged on both strategies and averaging the logit outputs from the two classifiers. It stays on CC200, so it should cost about 2× the current runtime, well below the CC400-driven timeout in round 3. I haven't run this version, so its Dev score is unknown.

I'm adding the anatomical AAL atlas (116 ROIs, including cerebellar parcels that matter in autism) as two more blocks, one per strategy (with and without GSR), using the same per-site re-centered tangent pipeline. Averaging across atlases was one of the most reliable gains in Abraham 2017, and AAL costs much less than the CC400 that timed out in round 3. The new blocks have fewer features, so each block's logistic-regression C is scaled to its feature count. Each block's logit is divided by the spread of its training-set logits before averaging, so blocks of different size get equal weight. I haven't run this version, so its Dev score is unknown.

L2 strength is currently fixed at C=0.001 for both the no-GSR and GSR blocks. The two strategies have different noise and correlation structure, so the best amount of shrinkage likely differs between them. I'll pick C separately for each block from a log grid, using grouped inner 5-fold CV on the training fold (grouped by `groups_train`). The selection criterion is within-site AUROC, the same metric the task is scored on, rather than a generic pooled score.

The two strategy blocks currently get equal weight in the average, even though GSR and no-GSR connectomes probably differ in how informative they are. This change reuses each block's inner-CV out-of-fold logits at its chosen C. It puts them on a common scale and picks simplex blend weights that maximize within-site AUROC, shrunk halfway toward equal weights to limit selection noise. Weaker blocks get down-weighted instead of diluting the ensemble, which is likely what hurt when AAL was added in round 6. I haven't run this version, so its Dev score is unknown.
